Dos grupos llevan el nombre de Family:
-El original,  rock progresivo de finales de los 60, principios de los 70 (más info más adelante).
-Un conjunto español posterior del principio de los 90 (más info a continuación).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
El grupo de Roger Chapman, mucho más antiguo y prolífico que el español, influenció otros grupos y cantantes tan notables como Jethro Tull (reconocido por el propio Anderson)

scenes.name: Prince y el sonido Mineápolis
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: Prince Rogers Nelson, hijo de músicos de Mineápolis, obtuvo de Warner el control creativo total a los diecisiete años y cambió la música del país como nadie desde James Brown. Arreglos desnudos como los de Rick James, voz de gospel, todos los instrumentos y un erotismo descarado («ningún negro jugaba así con la sensibilidad heterosexual desde Little Richard»): «Soft and Wet», «I Wanna Be Your Lover», «Head» de Dirty Mind (1980), «Erotic City». Warner lo vendió con Zapp como «New Black Funk». Controversy, 1999 («Let’s Work», «D.M.S.R.») y Purple Rain (1984), película y plataforma de satélites (Vanity, Apollonia, Sheila E., The Family). The Time de Morris Day («Cool», «777-9311», «Jungle Love») fijaron el listón de precisión del naked funk, y de ellos salieron Jesse Johnson y Jimmy Jam y Terry Lewis, productores de Janet Jackson, New Edition o S.O.S. Band. Luego vinieron mundos fantásticos al nivel de P-Funk o los Beatles (Around the World in a Day, Parade, Sign o’ the Times, Lovesexy). El psicólogo Alvin Poussaint lo llamó «flautista de Hamelín de una generación obsesionada por el sexo», quizá preparada así para el gangsta rap.

scenes.name: Rock progresivo
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Al emigrar a Gran Bretaña, el rock se convierte en mercancía de moda pero también se descontextualiza: lo que en EE UU era el diario de la juventud se vuelve en Gran Bretaña un ensayo. El progresivo no comenta la cultura juvenil sino que busca la innovación técnica: arranca con las óperas rock (S.F. Sorrow, Tommy) y los álbumes conceptuales, lo cimentan Traffic, Jeff Beck, Jethro Tull, Family y Genesis, y alcanza su cima con King Crimson (In The Court Of The Crimson King), Van Der Graaf Generator y Yes. Colosseum, la Third Ear Band (inventores de la world music), las variantes góticas (High Tide, Black Widow) y folk (Comus, Strawbs), Gentle Giant, Emerson Lake & Palmer y Roxy Music, que revoluciona el género y prepara la new wave y el synth-pop.

mentions.text: …the hoarse shout of Roger Chapman, one of the greatest rock vocalists of all times, and a sophisticated guitar-saxophone-violin dynamics, the Family borrowed from rhythm'n'blues, the music-hall, classical music and San Francisco's acid-rock to arrange their masterpiece, Music In A Doll's House…

xref.title: Early Life and Family (1962-1991)
xref.body: Dave Gahan's biological father, Jack, left the family when Dave was only six months old and died in 1991, just as Dave was attempting to reconnect with him. He was married to Joanne Fox, who helped establish the first official Depeche Mode fan club, and they had a son named Jack, but Dave rarely saw his son during the first five years of his life due to touring. "Dave also lost his biological father, Jack, who left the family when Dave was 6 months old."

xref.title: Cremation and Burial (1979)
xref.body: Following his death, Sid Vicious's family reportedly struggled to find a New York funeral home willing to take his body. He was eventually cremated in Jersey, and his ashes were spread on Nancy Spungen's grave in Philadelphia. "Apparently the family couldn't find a New York funeral home that would take his body, so he ended up being cremated into Jersey. His ashes were apparently spread on Nancy Spungens grave in Philadelphia."

xref.title: Depression and Personal Turmoil (April 1980)
xref.body: By April 1980, Ian Curtis was severely depressed, a state compounded not only by his epilepsy but also by a failing affair with a Belgian fan, the impending split from his wife, and dire financial difficulties that forced them to give away their family dog. He desired solitude but was ill-equipped to live alone. "By April 1980, Ian was very, very depressed. Not just as a result of the epilepsy either. He was having an affair with a Belgian fan. That wasn't going well. He and his wife were on the verge of splitting up. Money was so tight that they had to give away the family dog. He wanted to be alone but really wasn't equipped to live alone."

xref.title: Critique of Detective Tom Grant (Post-1994)
xref.body: Wendy Cobain, Kurt Cobain's mother, released a statement strongly criticizing Detective Tom Grant, who had been hired by the family to find Kurt when he was missing. She called Grant "inept," a "sleaze bag," and accused him of seeking "15 minutes of fame," also mentioning difficulties in getting him to sign a confidentiality form. "Tom Grant is the same inept private investigator who was hired by the family to find Kurt the week he was missing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mother's Dismissal of Tom Grant (Post-1994)
xref.body: Wendy Cobain, Kurt's mother, issued a statement dismissing Detective Tom Grant as an "inept private investigator" and a "sleaze bag." She accused him of trying to gain "15 minutes of fame" and noted that the family had unsuccessfully tried for months to get him to sign a confidentiality agreement. "Tom Grant is the same inept private investigator who was hired by the family to find Kurt the week he was missing."

xref.title: Stalker Death Threats (2004–) – Million-Dollar Security Overhaul, Threats to Kill Children
xref.body: Beginning in 2004, when his wife Vicki was six months pregnant with their first child, Chris Cornell received a sustained campaign of threatening letters and emails containing explicit, detailed descriptions of how Vicki and their children — Toni (age 3) and Christopher Jr. (age 1) — would be killed. The writer or writers demonstrated knowledge of the family's address at their Beverly Hills mansion. Messages included lines such as "you stole my baby and now the baby must die." The Cornells spent over a million dollars on security: fences, more than 40 closed-circuit video cameras, alarms, and 24-hour guards. "They spent more than a million dollars on security, fences, more than 40 close circuit video cameras, alarms, 24-hour guards."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Eddie Vedder's Return to Copenhagen (2007)
xref.body: On June 27, 2007, seven years after the Roskilde tragedy, Pearl Jam played at the Forum in Copenhagen. Eddie Vedder addressed the crowd from the stage, speaking about the impossibility of "closure" but the importance of connecting and learning from the loss. He specifically acknowledged the family of Frank Noens, one of the men who died at Roskilde, noting his mother Antoinette, sister Kathy, and friends were in attendance to celebrate his life, as a request from Kathy. "And I said, no, there's no closure. Is that the word in English? There's no closure. There's no end of the street."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death (2017)
xref.body: Gord Downie passed away on October 18, 2017. His death was met with widespread national mourning, with one poignant tweet summarizing the sentiment as "Canada closed, death in the family." "And when Gord died on October 18, 2017, it seemed like the whole country went into morning."

xref.title: Death by Suicide (July 20, 2017)
xref.body: On the morning of Thursday, July 20, 2017, at approximately 9 AM, a housekeeper found Chester Bennington hanging from a bedroom door at his house in Palos Verdes Estates. She alerted a driver who had arrived to pick him up for the TV commercial, and the driver subsequently called 911. "At around 9 a.m. on the morning of the 20th, a housekeeper found Chester hanging from a door in the bedroom."

xref.body: Gord Downie passed away on October 17, 2017, plunging the entire country into a period of profound mourning. A widely circulated social media post encapsulated the national sentiment: "Canada closed, death in the family." "And when he died on October 17, 2017, the whole country was thrown into mourning."

xref.title: AM Radio Preachers in the South
xref.body: During their travels through the South, the family would listen to preachers on AM radio late at night, often finding them "funny" or "not that smart of people," leading to good laughs. "he would also listen to him. If he came across someone that was preaching on the radio, we would listen to it and there were some funny, funny preachers."

xref.title: Autopsy Findings and Police Indifference
xref.body: An autopsy confirmed the presence of drugs but not in fatal amounts; however, it also revealed he was suffering from advanced leukemia, a previously unknown condition. Despite requests from his family to reinvestigate, New Orleans police showed no interest, and there were claims that the original police report was missing and the coroner had a history of falsifying autopsy results. "An autopsy was ordered and yes, he had drugs in the system but not in fatal amounts. They did find though that he was suffering from advanced leukemia, something that no one had known. The family asked the New Orleans cops to investigate again and again, but they just weren't interested. Some claim that the original police report is missing and that the corner had a rep for falsifying autopsy results."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Billy Joe Armstrong's Father's Death and Family Hardship
xref.body: Billy Joe's father passed away from cancer when Billy Joe was 10 years old. His mother, left to raise five children, worked as a waitress at Rod's Hickory Pit. A stepfather joined the family two years later, but all the children reportedly disliked him. "Billy Joe's father died of cancer when he was 10. He was just one of five kids being raised by a mother who could only find work as a waitress at a place called Rod's Hickory Pit."

xref.title: Birth and Childhood
xref.body: Rivers Cuomo was born in New York City to a hippie musician father and a hippie mother. He was raised in several Buddhist communities for the first ten years of his life, including an ashram called Yogaville, before his parents divorced in 1975, and the family settled in Connecticut. "Rivers was born in New York City. Dad was a hippie musician, and mum was a hippie hippie hippie."

His passing evoked widespread grief, with a poignant tweet at the time capturing the national sentiment: "Canada closed death in the family." xref.title: Developing Slap Bass Style
xref.body: Influenced by his jazz studies, Flea developed his distinctive slap bass style, which produced a new, jumpy, funky sound. He also studied Bootsy Collins, a favorite who played in George Clinton's band and Sly & The Family Stone. "Influenced by his years of jazz study Flea developed a style of slapping his bass, which gave everything a new jumpy funky sound."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Diplomat's Son – Real Name John Miller, Born in Ankara, Raised Across Multiple Postings
xref.body: Joe Strummer's entire punk persona was built on a working-class streetwise identity that contradicted his actual origins. His real name was John Mellor (referred to as John Miller in the podcast). He was born in Ankara, Turkey, while his father, a British diplomat with the Foreign Service, was posted there. His father subsequently received postings to Mexico City, Cairo, and Bonn, West Germany — providing Joe and his brother with security, good schools, and comfortable accommodations. The family eventually settled in Surrey, England, where the boys attended private schools befitting a diplomat's salary. Joe transformed himself into a punk musician via art school and spent the rest of his life distancing Joe Strummer the punk from his privileged origins. "He considered his upbringing to be an embarrassment."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Diverse Influences
xref.body: The band drew inspiration from a wide range of artists including James Brown, Funkadelic, Run DMC, Sly and the Family Stone, Led Zeppelin, Van Halen, and The Clash. "They were inspired equally by James Brown, Funkadelic, Run DMC, Slion the Family Stone, and Led Zeppelin Van Halen, and the Clash."

xref.title: Early Drumming Beginnings
xref.body: Neil Peart was born in Hamilton on September 12, 1952, and his first home was on the family dairy farm near Hager'sville. He started drumming at an early age, reportedly using chopsticks on his sister's playpen. The family later moved to St. Catharines, where at age 13, Neil began taking formal drum lessons using practice pads. After a year of committed practice, his parents bought him his first proper red drum kit. "Neil apparently liked to drum chopsticks on his sister's playpin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Life Trauma and Introduction to Piano
xref.body: Trent Reznor's parents divorced when he was six, leading him to live with his grandparents. This family trauma, alongside activities like skateboarding and building model trains, led him to the piano, which he began playing at five and showed immediate aptitude for. "Trent Rezner's parents divorced when he was just six. He went to live with his grandparents. The family trauma led him to a couple of things, skateboarding, building model trains, and playing the piano."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Life and Background
xref.body: Joe Strummer came from a privileged background, as his father was a diplomat. He was born in Turkey and lived in exotic places like Cairo and Mexico City before his family moved to England. He attended private schools and boarding school, and initially wanted to be a cartoonist. "He came from privilege. His dad was a diplomat and little Joe was born in Turkey and lived in exotic places like Cairo and Mexico City before the family moved to England."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rock Star Kids ｜ From the Archives

xref.title: Early Life and Engineering Background – War and Drums
xref.body: Jim Marshall was born in England in 1923. He initially worked in his family's fish and chip shop. Due to health reasons, he was unable to enlist in the war. Instead, he studied to become an engineer. During this time, he also turned to playing the drums and quickly became very proficient. "Jim Was born in England back in 1923 and for a while he worked in the family's fish and chip shop Unable to enlist in the war for health reasons he studied to be an engineer Any turn to the drums and Jim became very very good very very quickly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Life and Family Band
xref.body: Viola Smith was born in Wisconsin in 1912 and began playing drums at age 11. Her father ran a family band where each child was expected to pick up an instrument; drums became Viola's by default as all other instruments were taken. She started touring with the family band in the early 1920s. "Her father ran this band, featuring all the members of the family, and each kid was expected to pick up an instrument. And by the time he got to Viola, all the instruments were taken except the drums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

xref.title: Early Poverty of Ian Curtis
xref.body: While alive, singer Ian Curtis and his wife experienced severe poverty, reaching a point where they had to sell their family dog because they could no longer afford to feed it. "While he was alive, Ian was so poor that he and his wife had to sell the family dog because they couldn't afford to feed him."

xref.title: Fabrizio Moretti's Background
xref.body: Fabrizio Moretti was born in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. His father was a nuclear engineer who relocated the family to New York City. "And drummer for Brizio Mareti was born in Rio de Janeiro. His dad was a nuclear engineer who relocated the family to New York."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Family and Hockey Influence
xref.body: Gord's godfather was Harry Sinden, a family friend who later became the coach of Team Canada in the 1972 Canada-Russia series and subsequently worked as coach and general manager for the Boston Bruins. This connection influenced Gord's childhood passion for the Bruins, leading him to wear number four like Bobby Orr, before switching to play goal, a position he thoroughly enjoyed. "His godfather was Harry Sinden, a friend of the family. Harry would later go on to be the coach of Team Canada and the 72 Canada Russia series and then work as coach in GM with the Boston Bruins. And this is why as a kid, Gord was such a Bruins fan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: Win Butler's mother, Liza, was featured on The King Family Show, a variety program that aired on ABC in 1965, linking her directly to the family's musical television presence. "Wins Mom Liza was also on that show."

xref.title: Gordon Downie's Passing
xref.body: Gordon Downie, the lead singer, passed away on October 17th, 2017, marking one of the "saddest days in the history of Canadian music." His death followed a final tragically hip concert in Kingston on August 20th, 2016, which millions of Canadians watched knowing it would be the band's last live performance together due to his illness. The sentiment was widely captured by a tweet stating, "Canada closed, death in the family." "Canada closed, death in the family."

xref.title: Insane Family Life and Childhood
xref.body: His father, a religious extremist, threatened the family with death and dug graves in the basement of their New Hampshire log cabin to emphasize his seriousness. GG failed grade three, was bullied throughout school, and experimented with cross-dressing in high school. "Dad was a religious nut. He kept threatening the family with death. And to make sure they knew he was serious, he dug graves in the basement of their log cabin in New Hampshire. That's where you're gonna end up if you don't listen to me. Much insane family life ensued. GG failed grade three. He was bullied throughout school and experimented with cross dressing in high school."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Iroquois Heritage
xref.body: Joey Belladonna, the frontman for the metal band Anthrax, is part Iroquois, a heritage that comes from his mother's side of the family. "Joey Beladonna of Anthrex is part ear-acquod, his mother's side."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lineup Change and Family Involvement
xref.body: When The Jackson Five left Motown, Jermaine Jackson remained with the label and was replaced in the group by Randy Jackson, making for a total of six members over time. Beyond the core group, sisters Janet, Latoya, and Revy also factor into the family's musical presence, all overseen by their father, Joe Jackson. "When the group left Motown, Germain stayed behind and was replaced by Randy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Meeting Nancy's Parents – Philadelphia
xref.body: Sid and Nancy traveled to Philadelphia for Sid to meet Nancy's parents. The meeting was strained, and after a few hours, it was suggested the couple stay at a Holiday Inn instead of the family guest room. "They also went to Philadelphia, so Sid could meet the parents. That must have been interesting."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musical Uncle
xref.body: Alex Van Halen is the uncle of Wolfgang Van Halen, who played bass in the family band. "his dad and uncle's band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musical Uniqueness and Influences
xref.body: The Happy Mondays developed a completely unique sound, deliberately avoiding sounding like any one artist because they listened to a vast range of genres and artists, from Johnny Cash and Sly & The Family Stone to the Sex Pistols, The Band, William Ellison, The Rolling Stones, and The Beatles. This eclectic listening, coupled with their own perceived lack of traditional musical proficiency, resulted in a distinctive groove. "We just listened to everything. We didn't try it at the anyone, because we couldn't be, we weren't good enough."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Nomadic, Pentecostal Upbringing
xref.body: The Followill brothers and their cousin were raised in a strict, hardcore Pentecostal family, with their father serving as a preacher. The family, including their mother Betty Ann, lived a nomadic existence, traveling across the American South in an old Chrysler as their father delivered sermons. Due to a lack of funds for hotels, the family frequently camped out between services. The boys gained their foundational musical skills by singing gospel songs and playing drums during these church services. "The boys were brought up in a hardcore Pentecostal family. Dad was a preacher, and he, mother Betty Ann and the boys were pretty nomadic for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Thematic Structure of Everything Will Be All Right in the End
xref.body: The album "Everything Will Be All Right in the End" is divided into three thematic sections: "The Panopticon Artist," which explores the relationship between Weezer and their fans; "Belodona," comprising classic girl group-style songs; and "Patriarchia," songs about father figures. The "Patriarchia" theme is particularly significant as Rivers reconciled with his birth father, who left the family in 1975 and became a Pentecostal minister. "The album can be divided into three themes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
